title: How concrete sets and gets stronger
examples: Does concrete dry out to go hard?
Why do builders keep new concrete wet?

explain.say: Concrete is a mix of cement, water, sand and gravel. It does not harden by drying out: the cement reacts chemically with the water, called hydration, and within hours tiny crystals lock everything together.

draw.text: How concrete sets and gets stronger

explain.say: The reaction carries on for weeks. After 7 days a typical concrete has about 70 percent of its final strength, as more crystals grow into the gaps between the grains.
Engineers usually judge concrete at 28 days, when it should reach its design strength. They check by crushing sample cubes or cylinders in a powerful press.

New concrete must be kept damp while it cures, because if the water evaporates the reaction stops early and the surface becomes weak and cracks. Well-cured concrete keeps getting slightly stronger for years.

faq.a: No. Concrete hardens because cement reacts with water to form new crystals that bind the sand and gravel. It actually needs water to stay present, which is why it can even set underwater.
asks: Does concrete dry out to go hard?

faq.a: Hydration is the chemical reaction between cement and water. It forms a gel and needle-like crystals that grow, interlock and glue the mix into artificial rock, giving off heat as it goes.
asks: What happens when cement mixes with water?

faq.q: Why do builders keep new concrete wet?
faq.a: If water evaporates too soon, hydration stops before the concrete is strong, and the surface shrinks and cracks. Builders spray it, cover it with plastic or wet sheets, or use curing compounds for the first days.

faq.q: Why is concrete tested at 28 days?
faq.a: By 28 days most concrete has gained nearly all its strength, so it became the standard age for checking that a mix meets its design. Samples are crushed in a press and the force is measured.
asks: How strong is concrete after a week?

faq.a: Yes. Because it hardens by chemical reaction rather than drying, concrete can set underwater, which is how bridge piers and harbour walls are built. The Romans made sea walls this way too.

facts: Joseph Aspdin patented Portland cement in 1824.
Concrete is the most widely used human-made material on Earth.
Hydrating cement gives off heat, so very large pours such as dams are cooled with embedded water pipes.

quiz.why: Hydration forms crystals that bind the mix; the concrete needs the water to react.

wrong.1: Drying out too early actually stops the hardening.
wrong.2: Nothing melts; it is a chemical reaction at normal temperature.
